Flow.description:
WHAT IT DOES: Answers one question: which Household does this person already belong to? Give it a Contact Id, an email address, or both, and it returns the Household Account and its Party Relationship Group, or nothing when the person is new or in no Household.
HOW IT WORKS, STEP BY STEP: 1. If you passed a Contact Id, it goes straight to the memberships. If you only passed an email, it first finds the Person Account with that email; no match means the person is new, and the flow returns empty-handed (that is an answer, not an error). 2. Reads the person's active memberships. Only indirect relations are considered, because a Person Account's direct relation points at itself, never at a Household. 3. Collects the Account Ids of those memberships with a small transform, then asks in ONE query which of them carries an active Household group, oldest first. That sort matters: a person in two Households is answered with the one they joined first. 4. Returns the Household's Account Id. The group record itself deliberately never leaves this flow: a populated Party Relationship Group crossing a subflow's output boundary crashes the packaged (managed) runtime with an internal Salesforce error, so callers get the Id and query what more they need.
WHERE IT FITS: The NPC Account engine calls this when Contact 1 of a Household-mode form has just converted and the submission has no Account yet: a returning family keeps the Household they have instead of getting a duplicate. It is form-agnostic and read-only, so it is safe to call from anywhere. It never writes logs; it returns HasError and ErrorMessage instead.
